documents.title: Ophthalmology — baseline hydroxychloroquine exam
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Eye clinic report, exam 1/10/2024
Indication: baseline exam, hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily started 11/2023 for RA.

VA cc 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pupils equal and reactive, no afferent defect. IOP normal both eyes. Anterior segment quiet. Dilated fundus: healthy optic nerves, flat maculae with normal foveal reflex, normal vessels and periphery OU.
SD-OCT macula: normal foveal contour, intact ellipsoid zone both eyes.
Humphrey 10-2: reliable, full both eyes.

Impression: normal baseline exam, no retinopathy.
Plan: annual screening can begin after 5 years of use given her dose and normal kidney function, sooner if risk factors change.

Ophthalmology

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Rheumatology clinic — follow-up note, 03/04/2024

RA, seropositive, erosive. On hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily since late November, prednisone taper finished in January.

She is much improved. Morning stiffness about 15 minutes, no swelling she can see, back to typing all day. No fevers. Weight stable.

Exam: no synovitis in hands, wrists, elbows, shoulders, knees or feet. Full fist both hands.

ESR 18 mm/hr, CRP 0.6 mg/dL today.

Assessment: good response to hydroxychloroquine monotherapy. Baseline eye exam in January was normal.
Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily. We will not add a second agent while she stays in this range. Recheck here in 6-12 months, sooner with any flare.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Office Visit — Pruritus and Jaundice
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Booked herself in after a coworker told her she looked yellow. Itching since roughly May, all over, much worse at night — up scratching, sleeping badly. Tried cetirizine and diphenhydramine from the drugstore with no effect. Over the last two months she has noticed her skin and the whites of her eyes yellowing. Tired for months, which she had put down to work. No abdominal pain, no fevers, no change in stool color she has noticed. No alcohol ever. No new meds or supplements; skin creams are her usual ones. No travel.

Meds: levothyroxine 125 mcg, estradiol patch 0.05 twice weekly, progesterone 200 mg days 1-12, hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily, topical clobetasol and triamcinolone PRN.

O: Afebrile, vitals normal. Clearly icteric skin and sclerae. Excoriations on forearms and shins. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver edge palpable below the right costal margin, no spleen felt, no ascites. No asterixis.

A: Jaundice with pruritus, presumably cholestatic. Long list of autoimmune disease in her and her family puts PBC high on the list; obstruction has to be excluded.

P:
- Hepatic panel, INR, CBC, BMP now (stat to the lab).
- RUQ ultrasound.
- Urgent GI referral.
- Will call her tonight or tomorrow with results.

documents.title: Results — liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called patient with yesterday's results. Total bili 2.8, direct 1.5, alk phos 420, AST 80, ALT 75 — cholestatic pattern. INR 1.0. CBC and BMP fine. Added AMA; she'll come in tomorrow morning for the draw. Ultrasound scheduled 11/12. GI has her 11/18 — told her to call us if she gets abdominal pain, fever, confusion or dark tarry stool before then.

documents.title: AMA positive
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Antimitochondrial antibody positive. With the cholestatic panel this points strongly to primary biliary cholangitis. Forwarded to GI ahead of 11/18 visit. Portal message to patient: the antibody test supports the diagnosis we talked about; GI will go over treatment next week.

reports.text:
Indication: jaundice, cholestatic liver tests.
Liver: enlarged, 19 cm in craniocaudal length, with normal homogeneous echotexture and smooth contour. No focal lesion. Hepatic and portal veins patent with normal flow direction.
Biliary: no intrahepatic biliary dilatation. Common bile duct 4 mm. Gallbladder normally distended without stones, sludge or wall thickening. Sonographic Murphy sign negative.
Pancreas: visualized portions unremarkable.
Spleen: normal size.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Hepatomegaly with normal echotexture. No biliary dilatation or gallstones. No ascites.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

medications.drug_text: cholestyramine resin 4000 MG Powder for Oral Suspension
medications.sig: Mix 1 packet (4 g) in water and take once daily; take at least 4 hours apart from levothyroxine and ursodiol

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology & Hepatology — Consultation
Visit 11/18/2024

Thank you for the urgent referral of Ms. Winslow, 50, who carries a history of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine, hypothyroidism, discoid lupus, lichen planus and rheumatoid arthritis.

For about six months she has been tired and itchy, the itch worst at night and not touched by over-the-counter antihistamines. For two months her skin has been turning yellow.

Medications: levothyroxine 125 mcg daily, hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily, estradiol patch with cyclic progesterone, topical steroids.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: no alcohol history of any kind; no recent travel; no high-risk sexual exposures. Never smoker.
Family: mother RA, father hypothyroidism and colon cancer, sister SLE.

Examination: afebrile, vital signs normal. Skin and sclerae icteric. Liver enlarged to palpation; no splenomegaly, no ascites. Murphy's sign negative.

Data reviewed from your office:
  Total bilirubin 2.8 mg/dL, direct 1.5 mg/dL
  Alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (40-120)
  AST 80 U/L (10-40), ALT 75 U/L (7-56)
  INR 1.0
  Antimitochondrial antibody: positive
  RUQ ultrasound 11/12: hepatomegaly, normal echotexture, no ductal dilatation, no stones

Impression: Primary biliary cholangitis. A cholestatic profile, positive AMA and a non-obstructed biliary tree make the diagnosis without a biopsy. Hydroxychloroquine is not a convincing culprit for this pattern.

Plan:
1. Ursodiol 500 mg twice daily (about 14 mg/kg/day).
2. Cholestyramine 4 g daily for the itch. She must separate it by at least 4 hours from levothyroxine and ursodiol — reviewed a schedule with her (levothyroxine on waking, ursodiol with breakfast and dinner, cholestyramine mid-afternoon).
3. I would stop systemic hormone therapy while she is jaundiced; I will leave that with you.
4. Liver panel in 3 months, then follow-up here.
5. Baseline DXA — PBC carries bone-loss risk.
6. Confirm hepatitis A/B immunity and vaccinate as needed.

With thanks,
Gastroenterology

documents.body:
GI letter in: PBC, started ursodiol and cholestyramine. Called Jill — she has both from the pharmacy and has the timing written on her fridge. Per GI, stopping the estradiol patch and progesterone now. She's fine with it; hot flashes have been mild this year. Warned she may get some vasomotor symptoms back and her cycles will go back to her own pattern.
Also: off estrogen her levothyroxine requirement can shift, so TSH/FT4 in 8 weeks, plus hep B surface antibody (GI wants immunity checked). Orders in.

Indication: screening; first-degree relative (father) with colon cancer at 65; prior colonoscopy 2015 normal.

documents.title: Office Visit — Fatigue and Weight Gain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since about April she's felt like she's moving through mud. Exhausted by mid-afternoon, cold all the time even in July, constipated for the first time in her life, cramps in her calves at night, and she says her thinking at work is sluggish — losing track of what she was doing. Up about 13 lb without eating differently. Periods have gone light and irregular since spring. Taking levothyroxine 125 every morning, nothing near it; ursodiol twice daily. No cholestyramine since February. No itching. Mood OK, just tired.

O: Pulse low 60s, BP normal. Weight 78.6 kg. Skin dry. Not icteric. No thyroid tissue. Heart slow-regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

PHQ-9: 4.

A: Fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation — reads like under-replacement, but she has been stable on this dose. Perimenopausal transition also in the mix for the cycles.

P:
- BMP, TSH, CBC, hepatic panel today.
- Results to her this afternoon.

Addendum 17:30: Na 132 (mild hyponatremia), rest of BMP normal. TSH 1.4 — normal. CBC normal. ALP 165, bili 0.8, still coming down. TSH doesn't explain how she feels; with her RAI history I'd like endo to look. Referral placed back to her endocrinologist; asked them to see her this month. Called and explained.

documents.title: Endocrinology visit
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology — clinic note
Seen 7/31/2025, referred back by primary care

Ms. Winslow, 50, with Graves' disease treated by radioactive iodine and hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 125 mcg daily. I last saw her in 2022 for fatigue and cold intolerance, which settled after her estrogen was moved to a patch. She has since been diagnosed with discoid lupus, lichen planus, RA and PBC.

Over four months: progressive fatigue, cold intolerance and a 6-kg weight gain. New constipation, muscle cramps, and what she calls sluggish thinking at work. Menses scant and irregular. No neck pain.

Medications: levothyroxine 125 mcg daily, ursodiol 500 mg twice daily, hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily, topical steroids.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 110/70, HR 58.
Skin cool and dry. Ankle jerks show delayed relaxation. Thyroid not palpable, not tender. Visual fields by confrontation in clinic: bitemporal peripheral loss.

Primary care's BMP of 7/14 is normal except mild hyponatremia (Na 132). TSH there 1.4.

Thyroid function drawn today; I will write again with results and a plan.

Endocrinology

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning on an empty stomach

documents.title: Endocrinology results letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology — results and plan, 8/4/2025

Dear Doctor,

Thyroid tests from 7/31: TSH 1.2 mIU/L, free T4 0.6 ng/dL (0.8-1.8).

Free T4 is low and the TSH is not raised to meet it. In someone with no meaningful thyroid of her own after RAI, that is the picture of central hypothyroidism: the pituitary is no longer driving the TSH response, and the TSH you checked on 7/14 was falsely reassuring. From here on her dose should be adjusted to free T4, not TSH.

Plan:
1. Levothyroxine increased to 137 mcg daily. New prescription sent.
2. Free T4 (with TSH for completeness) in 6 weeks; she can have it drawn at her physical in September.
3. Follow-up here in about a year.

I have explained to her that the dose change should help the fatigue and cold intolerance over several weeks.

Endocrinology

documents.title: New thyroid dose
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The endocrinologist raised my thyroid pill to 137. Do I just finish the old 125 bottle first or start the new one right away? And can I still get the blood test at my physical in September or do I need a separate visit?

documents.title: RE: New thyroid dose
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Start the 137 tomorrow morning and set the 125s aside. Your physical is a good time for the blood test — I'll make sure free T4 is on the order. I've updated your medication list here.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical, first in two years (missed last fall, then the liver workup took over).

Interval history:
- PBC (GI, Nov 2024): on ursodiol, itch gone, ALP down to 165 in July. Off cholestyramine since Feb. DXA in March normal. Hep B series done.
- Hormone therapy stopped Nov 2024 at GI's suggestion.
- Central hypothyroidism (endo, Aug 2025): FT4 low with a normal TSH; levothyroxine to 137. Six weeks on it now — less wiped out in the afternoons, still not herself.
- RA quiet on hydroxychloroquine; rheum yearly.
- Colonoscopy April: normal, next 2035.
- Skin: DLE and LP quiet.
LMP in July; cycles had been light and irregular since spring.

Meds: levothyroxine 137 mcg daily, ursodiol 500 mg BID, hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily, clobetasol 0.05% oint and triamcinolone 0.1% cream PRN.
NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal. Weight 79.4 kg. Not icteric. Skin without active plaques. Neck no nodes. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, liver edge not felt today. Joints without synovitis. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix; Pap/HPV collected. No edema.

A/P
1. Central hypothyroidism on 137 mcg: FT4 (and TSH) today; endo dosing to FT4.
2. Hyponatremia in July (132): recheck with CMP.
3. PBC: per GI; LFTs in CMP.
4. RA, DLE, LP: per specialists.
5. HM: Pap/HPV today. Mammogram overdue — ordered. PCV20 today (chronic liver disease). Flu and COVID today.
6. Irregular menses then none since July at 50 — likely the menopausal transition.

PHQ-2: 1.

Addendum 9/16 16:00: Na 137. FT4 1.0, TSH 0.9 on 137 mcg. CMP otherwise normal; ALP within the range GI expects on ursodiol. CBC, lipids fine. Copy to endo.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jill, your Pap came back normal and the HPV test was negative, so the next one isn't due for five years. Everything else from your physical I sent last week. Don't forget the mammogram — the order is in.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Hepatology — 1-year review, 11/10/2025

PBC diagnosed November 2024, on ursodiol 500 mg twice daily (about 13 mg/kg at her current weight). No itch, no jaundice. She reports a diagnosis of central hypothyroidism this summer with a levothyroxine increase.

Exam: anicteric, no stigmata of chronic liver disease, no ascites.

Today: ALP 150 U/L, total bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL.

Assessment: adequate biochemical response to ursodiol at one year (ALP under 1.67 times the upper limit, normal bilirubin). No second-line therapy needed.
Plan: continue ursodiol; liver panel every 6 months through primary care or here; hepatology review yearly.

Gastroenterology
